transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (CTO - NimbusHealth), Priya Nair (Head of Security - NimbusHealth), Carlos Mendez (Infra Lead - NimbusHealth), Aisha Rahman (Compliance)

Summary:
NimbusHealth is a healthcare SaaS evaluating Redwood for inference serving. Main focus is security posture: SOC 2/ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency and retention. They are sensitive due to PHI and want to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, compliance artifacts, and integration steps.

Topics:
- Compliance artifacts (SOC 2, ISO) and evidence
- SSO/SAML and IdP integration
- RBAC and least-privilege roles for model access
- Audit logging and retention lengths
- Encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM options
- Data residency and VPC/private deployments, HIPAA considerations
- Next steps: docs, demo, security deep-dive and pricing

Action items (refer to metadata list above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros from our side, i'm lena, AE, and with me ravi and maya on the security and infra side.
[00:10] Jared (Nimbus CTO): hi all, Jared here. we're excited to see how Redwood might fit, especially for inference hosting of our clinical models. big question for us is security and compliance around PHI.
[00:20] Priya (Nimbus Sec): Priya — heading security. main things: SOC 2, iso 27001, SSO, audit logs, and obviously encryption/KMS. we'll also want to see how data retention and deletion works, and any egress controls.
[00:33] Ravi (Redwood SE): great, thanks. quick frame: we'll cover how hosted, dedicated, and private options map to compliance and controls, then go into SSO/SAML, RBAC, logs, and encryption. feel free to stop and ask specifics.
[00:48] Carlos (Infra): timeline: we're looking to pick a vendor in the next 6-8 weeks, pilot in staging in ~2 months. need to know if we can get dedicated or private earlier for PHI.
[00:58] Maya (Redwood): noted. for PHI we usually recommend Dedicated or Private; hosted can be fine with contractual safeguards but many healthcare customers prefer isolated capacity or private deployments.
[01:12] Priya: can you be explicit — for hosted, do you have SOC 2 and do you sign BAAs?
[01:22] Lena: yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and we provide a BAA for customers handling PHI. i'll send the report after this call. (slight pause) the hosted API is SOC 2 covered, but for maximum isolation Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and private networking; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you customer-managed control plane.
[01:44] Priya: what about ISO 27001? we've got customers requesting that too.
[01:49] Ravi: we're in process on ISO; some parts of the platform map to ISO controls, and we can share our security program summary. but SOC 2 is the primary attestation we provide today.
[02:05] Aisha (Compliance): can you explain audit logs — what's captured, retention, and access controls?
[02:12] Maya: sure. we capture request/response metadata (not full persisted response bodies for hosted by default), user access events, admin changes, model deploy/rollout events. retention is configurable in Dedicated and Private; hosted has default retention window (we'll share specifics in the SOC/docs). you can export logs to your splunk/datadog or to s3 if you have dedicated storage endpoints.
[02:40] Carlos: export to our s3 in our account? we want logs to live in our account for compliance.
[02:46] Ravi: with Private deployments or Dedicated with specific integrations we can route logs to a customer-owned s3 or SIEM. hosted can send events to a customer webhook or SIEM but not the same as customer-managed s3 by default.
[02:59] Priya: encryption — at rest and in transit? who holds keys?
[03:05] Lena: all traffic TLS in transit. at rest we encrypt using keys managed by Redwood by default, but for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS, Google KMS) and HSM integrations for keys if required.
[03:24] Priya: do you support bring-your-own-kms (BYOK)?
[03:27] Ravi: yes, BYOK for Dedicated and Private is supported. hosted supports CMEK for certain plans — we'll confirm exact tiers in the followup.
[03:39] Jared: about RBAC — we need fine-grained controls so only a handful of services can call production models, and dev teams shouldn't access prod keys.
[03:48] Maya: Redwood Console has role-based access controls with predefined roles and custom roles. you can reduce scope by route/model level controls, token scoping, and can integrate with SSO to map groups to roles.
[04:02] Priya: SSO — we use Okta and Azure AD. is SAML 2.0 supported? any SCIM for group sync?
[04:10] Ravi: SAML 2.0 is supported for SSO. SCIM group sync is supported for Dedicated and Private — hosted supports SSO and SCIM on enterprise plans. we'll include the SAML metadata and a quickstart.
[04:29] Carlos: regarding data residency — some customers require EU-only storage; can you pin region for hosted?
[04:35] Lena: yes, hosted has region selection for many models and data residency options; Dedicated and Private obviously provide more control — Private can be fully in your VPC/region or on-prem.
[04:48] Priya: retention and deletion — how do we ensure that when we delete datasets or tokens you scrubs?
[04:55] Ravi: we have deletion APIs and retention controls; for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to meet your policies, and for hosted we have standard retention windows, and can offer shorter retention on contract. deletion requests are logged and we can provide attestations. we'll share the deletion API docs.
[05:12] Jared: do you store KV cache/prefixes? some of our prompts could include PHI in context; where is that cached?
[05:19] Maya: good callout. KV cache is ephemeral and stays on the serving nodes; for hosted we have automatic TTLs and don't persist beyond configured retention. for Dedicated/Private you can configure cache persistence and encryption settings. we recommend not sending PHI in prompts when possible, but if you do, we can route those requests to private deployments.
[05:41] Priya: what about incident response and breach notification for PHI?
[05:45] Lena: we have an incident response plan; SLA'd notification timelines are in the contract. we'll include IR playbooks and contact points in the followup.
[05:55] Aisha: do you support audit log immutability or append-only logs for compliance?
[06:00] Ravi: for Dedicated/Private we can enable append-only logging and ship to customer-owned immutable storage (e.g., S3 with Object Lock). hosted has retained logs but immutability is part of enterprise features.
[06:16] Priya: encryption keys lifecycle — what's rotation policy and access audit?
[06:21] Maya: when using customer-managed KMS, rotation is controlled by your KMS policies; we record key use in audit logs. for Redwood-managed keys we rotate on a regular cadence and can provide rotation docs.
[06:34] Jared: any third-party pen test reports or bug bounty info?
[06:38] Lena: yes we do regular third-party pen tests and have a security vulnerability disclosure program. we'll share summary reports and the contact for our security team.
[06:50] Priya: HIPAA specifically — you mentioned BAA. do you have customers live with PHI on hosted?
[06:57] Ravi: some customers run PHI on Dedicated or Private; hosted is used with BAAs and contractual controls but many healthcare customers prefer Dedicated/Private for data isolation. we'll share examples and references (redacted).
[07:14] Carlos: for private deployment — how much lead time and what infra do you need on our side?
[07:20] Maya: private can be on-prem or VPC. typical lead time 6-8 weeks depending on infra readiness. we provide deployment manifests, helm charts, and our ops runbook. we also offer a managed private option where we co-manage the control plane.
[07:38] Priya: logging format — can we get structured event logs with trace ids to tie back to our observability?
[07:44] Ravi: yes, we emit structured JSON logs with trace IDs, model IDs, route IDs, and request metadata; we can map trace ids to your request ids if you pass them in headers.
[07:57] Jared: performance/latency — when we move to Dedicated, can you guarantee latencies? we need p50/p95 targets for SLAs.
[08:04] Maya: Dedicated comes with predictable capacity SLAs. we'll include sample latency profiles and metrics. actual SLA numbers are in the enterprise contract.
[08:15] Priya: can you redact or mask PHI automatically? any built-in PII detection?
[08:20] Ravi: we have content filters and PII detectors available as opt-in features; masking/redaction pipelines can be configured but typically customers run local pre-processing to strip PHI before sending. we can discuss built-in redaction for the private deployments.
[08:40] Aisha: legal/procurement asks — do you support contractual security addendums, audit rights, and penetration testing by our third party?
[08:48] Lena: yes we can accommodate security addendums; audit rights are handled via scope and NDA; third-party pen tests usually coordinated with our security team — we'll share the process.
[08:58] Priya: does Redwood maintain an asset inventory and CMDB info we can tie into?
[09:03] Maya: we maintain internal asset registers; we can provide summaries and SOC evidence mapping but full CMDB access is not typical — we can discuss what evidence you need.
[09:16] Jared: any data egress controls? we want to block model outputs that contain patient identifiers from leaving our region.
[09:24] Ravi: you can implement output filters and configure routing policies; with Private we can ensure data never leaves your VPC/region. hosted can be region-pinned for many use cases.
[09:37] Priya: Could you share an architecture diagram for each deployment mode?
[09:41] Lena: yes we'll attach diagrams — hosted, dedicated, private, and network flow examples.
[09:47] Carlos: what's the minimal set of credentials/services we need to enable during onboarding?
[09:52] Maya: for Dedicated you need an AWS account role for provisioning, KMS keys if BYOK, VPC peering or private link details; we'll provide a checklist.
[10:03] Jared: ok let's talk about the specifics of SAML set up — how to map groups to roles, and SCIM.
[10:09] Ravi: you can map IdP groups to Redwood roles; SCIM will sync groups and users. we'll send our SCIM schema and mapping examples.
[10:19] Priya: logs retention length — what are default windows and max?
[10:24] Maya: hosted default logs retention is 90 days; Dedicated/Private can be configured for longer retention and archived to customer storage indefinitely.
[10:35] Aisha: do you have certified encryption algorithms and FIPS compliance?
[10:40] Ravi: we use industry standard algorithms (AES-256) and can support FIPS 140-2 validated modules when integrating with customer HSMs.
[10:50] Priya: for compliance review we'll need control mappings. do you provide an SOC control mapping to common frameworks (HIPAA, ISO, NIST)?
[10:57] Lena: yes we provide mappings and a control matrix that shows coverage against NIST 800-53, HIPAA, and ISO where applicable. we'll include that in the followup.
[11:10] Jared: is there any support for data classification labels embedded in requests so you can route or restrict certain traffic?
[11:16] Maya: yes you can pass metadata headers or tags and we have routing policies that can route to private pools if a classification flag is present.
[11:26] Priya: what about developer ergonomics — how do we audit which engineer called what model and what output?
[11:33] Ravi: full audit trails are available in the Console; each API token usage is logged with user context when SSO is enabled. we can forward those logs to your SIEM for longer retention.
[11:46] Carlos: for POC — can we run a short benchmark with our dataset in your staging environment and measure latency and cost?
[11:52] Lena: yes — typical POC: we set up a dedicated staging pool or private trial, run throughput/latency benchmarks, and share the results and cost estimates.
[12:02] Jared: ok, procurement will ask for pricing and terms — what's typical for Dedicated vs Private?
[12:08] Maya: Dedicated is reserved capacity pricing with monthly/annual commits; Private has platform licensing + deployment fees. we'll send a starter range in the followup.
[12:17] Priya: last question — are there any known limitations for HIPAA where you advise customers not to use certain features?
[12:24] Ravi: generally avoid sending PHI into public shared pools; use dedicated/private or pre-process. some experimental features that cache outputs may be disabled for PHI workloads. we'll enumerate these restrictions.
[12:38] Lena: recap: we'll send SOC 2 report + control matrix, SAML/SCIM quickstart, architecture diagrams, deletion API and log export docs, and a proposal for Dedicated and Private pricing. we'll also schedule a technical deep dive to scope private deployment.
[12:54] Jared: sounds good — thanks all.
[12:58] Priya: thanks — appreciate the detail.
[13:02] Aisha: thanks, bye.

[44:30] END OF RECORDING

Notes: transcript contains occasional speaker overlaps and minor auto-transcription errors (names/acronyms may be slightly off). references to configuration tiers and exact retention windows will be confirmed in follow-up documentation.
